follow-up time: Until achievement of independent oral feeding
exposure: Gestational age (<29 weeks, 29-33 weeks, late preterm)
Neonatal morbidities (necrotizing enterocolitis, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, severe intraventricular hemorrhage)
outcome: Post-menstrual age at achievement of independent oral feeding
cohort: 2700 preterm infants born before 37 weeks gestational age admitted to a level III NICU between January 1978 and July 2013
finding: The mean post-menstrual age at achievement of independent oral feeding was 36 + 4/7 weeks, with gestational age under 29 weeks and major morbidities being associated with delays, while vaginal delivery and advancements in neonatal care were associated with earlier achievement.
mod_finding: Preterm infants delivered vaginally achieved independent oral feeding three days sooner than infants delivered via c-section (p < 0.0001).
